# nuxt-backend/test-utils

**`Experimental`**

Test helpers for an app's Vue side — `nuxt-backend/test-utils`:
[createBackendMock](#createbackendmock), a fake backend and session that the package's
composables and components, and the base module's, read in a component or
page test; [resetBackendMock](#resetbackendmock), which forgets it;
[backendMockProvides](#backendmockprovides), what a plain `mount()` provides it with;
[backendTestAliases](#backendtestaliases), the Vitest aliases that point them at it, so a
test needs no `vi.mock`; and [renderEmail](#renderemail), which renders an email
the package sends as your `setupEmail` options would. Your Convex functions
are tested with `nuxt-backend/test` instead.

Experimental: the mock answers the way the auth and billing flows answer
today, and follows them as they move.

## Functions

### backendTestAliases()

```ts
function backendTestAliases(): Record<string, string>;
```

Defined in: [src/runtime/test-utils/aliases.ts](https://github.com/qruto/nuxt-backend/blob/main/src/runtime/test-utils/aliases.ts)

**`Experimental`**

Vite aliases that put [createBackendMock](#createbackendmock) under the package's
composables and components and the base module's own. Three imports are
swapped:

- `#convex/auth-client`, the Better Auth client the session layer is built
  on (`useAuth`, `useBetterAuth`, the page guard), for one that
  answers from the mock;
- `nuxt-convex-module/client` and `nuxt-convex-module/vue`, for the base
  module's own entry with every export kept, whose composables also
  provide the mock where a plain `mount()` needs it.

Two private names reach the base module's real files for those stand-ins.
With the aliases in a Vitest project, a test needs no `vi.mock`.

Use them in a project with `@nuxt/test-utils`' `nuxt` environment
(`defineVitestProject`, or `defineVitestConfig` for a single project): it
transforms the package and the base module, which is where the aliases
apply. Keep tests that need a live deployment in a project without them.

#### Returns

`Record`\<`string`, `string`\>

#### Example

```ts [vitest.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config'
import { defineVitestProject } from '@nuxt/test-utils/config'
import { backendTestAliases } from 'nuxt-backend/test-utils'

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    projects: [
      await defineVitestProject({
        resolve: { alias: backendTestAliases() },
        test: { name: 'app', include: ['test/app/*.test.ts'], environment: 'nuxt' },
      }),
    ],
  },
})
```

### renderEmail()

```ts
function renderEmail<Name>(
   name, 
   data, 
   options?
): Promise<EmailMessage>;
```

Defined in: [src/runtime/test-utils/email.ts](https://github.com/qruto/nuxt-backend/blob/main/src/runtime/test-utils/email.ts)

**`Experimental`**

Render one of the emails the package sends, as `setupEmail` with the same
options would send it, without a deployment: the template in effect (an
override in `templates`, else the packaged one) in the shared layout, in
`locale` read through `messages`. Pass the options your
`backend/email.ts` gives `setupEmail` (`templates`, `messages`,
`defaultLocale`, `localePaths`, `brand`, `theme`) to test what your users get.
Experimental, with the rest of `nuxt-backend/test-utils`.

#### Type Parameters

| Type Parameter |
| ------ |
| <a id="type-parameter-name"></a> `Name` *extends* keyof [`EmailTemplates`](/docs/reference/api/email#emailtemplates) |

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `name` | `Name` |
| `data` | [`EmailTemplateData`](/docs/reference/api/email#emailtemplatedata)\<`Name`\> |
| `options?` | [`RenderEmailOptions`](#renderemailoptions) |

#### Returns

`Promise`\<[`EmailMessage`](/docs/reference/api/email#emailmessage)\>

#### Example

```ts
import { renderEmail } from 'nuxt-backend/test-utils'
import de from '../i18n/locales/de.json'

const message = await renderEmail('welcome', { email: 'ada@example.com', name: 'Ada' }, { locale: 'de', messages: { de } })
expect(message.subject).toBe('Willkommen')
```

### createBackendMock()

```ts
function createBackendMock(init?): BackendMock;
```

Defined in: [src/runtime/test-utils/mock.ts](https://github.com/qruto/nuxt-backend/blob/main/src/runtime/test-utils/mock.ts)

**`Experimental`**

A fake backend for an app's component and page tests: the package's
composables and components, and the base module's own (`useQuery`,
`<Authenticated>`, the page guard, …), read it instead of a
deployment once [backendTestAliases](#backendtestaliases) is in the Vitest project.
Queries answer from `state.queries`; mutations, actions and auth client
calls are recorded in `calls` and answer what `stub` says (or a built-in
answer for the auth flows: signing in, switching workspace, …); `fail`
makes any of them fail. The state is reactive: change it in a test and
the rendered page follows.

The newest mock is the one everything reads, so make one per test, in a
`beforeEach` or the test itself. Signed out unless `user` is given.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| ------ | ------ | ------ |
| `init?` | [`BackendMockInit`](#backendmockinit) | The starting state: the account, its workspaces, query results. |

#### Returns

[`BackendMock`](#backendmock)

#### Example

```ts
import { createBackendMock } from 'nuxt-backend/test-utils'
import { mountSuspended } from '@nuxt/test-utils/runtime'
import { flushPromises } from '@vue/test-utils'
import { expect, test } from 'vitest'
import CreditsPage from '~/pages/credits.vue'

test('the balance follows the backend', async () => {
  const backend = createBackendMock({
    user: { name: 'Ada' },
    queries: { 'billing:getCredits': { meters: [{ meterId: 'm1', name: 'credits', balance: 42 }] } },
  })
  const page = await mountSuspended(CreditsPage)
  expect(page.text()).toContain('42')

  backend.state.queries['billing:getCredits'] = { meters: [{ meterId: 'm1', name: 'credits', balance: 0 }] }
  await flushPromises()
  expect(page.text()).toContain('0')
})
```

### resetBackendMock()

```ts
function resetBackendMock(): void;
```

Defined in: [src/runtime/test-utils/mock.ts](https://github.com/qruto/nuxt-backend/blob/main/src/runtime/test-utils/mock.ts)

**`Experimental`**

Forget every mock: the active one, the signed-out fallback and the
session token the auth layer cached. The next read answers from a fresh
signed-out mock until a test makes its own.

#### Returns

`void`

### backendMockProvides()

```ts
function backendMockProvides(): Record<symbol, unknown>;
```

Defined in: [src/runtime/test-utils/mock.ts](https://github.com/qruto/nuxt-backend/blob/main/src/runtime/test-utils/mock.ts)

**`Experimental`**

The mock's client and auth state under the base module's keys and its
function tree under this package's, for a plain `mount()`: `mountSuspended` copies them from the
Nuxt app, where each new mock is provided, but `mount()` starts an app of
its own. Pass them as `global.provide`. Throws when the aliases are not in
the Vitest project.

#### Returns

`Record`\<`symbol`, `unknown`\>

#### Example

```ts
import { mount } from '@vue/test-utils'
import { backendMockProvides, createBackendMock } from 'nuxt-backend/test-utils'

createBackendMock({ user: { name: 'Ada' } })
const page = mount(Dashboard, { global: { provide: backendMockProvides() } })
```
